claim:
Let \(X=\mathrm{ces}_2^{(2)}\) be the real plane with
\[
\|(x,y)\|_X
=
\left(
x^2+\left(\frac{|x|+|y|}{2}\right)^2
\right)^{1/2}.
\]
Then its Dunkl--Williams constant is
\[
DW(X)=\sqrt{\frac{32}{5}}=\frac{8}{\sqrt{10}}.
\]
After the linear normalization
\[
M(s,t)=\sqrt{s^2+t^2+\frac{2}{\sqrt5}|st|},
\]
the smooth points of the unit sphere contribute at most \(\sqrt5\) to \(DW\), while the sharp value is generated at a coordinate-axis point by Birkhoff--James directions \((r,1)\) with \(r\downarrow0\).
integrity: The proof is exact and exhaustive: the published Birkhoff--James midpoint characterization reduces the calculation to smooth elliptical arcs and coordinate axes, and both cases are controlled by explicit quadratic sublevel intervals.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is restricted to the real two-dimensional Cesàro space at exponent 2. It does not determine other finite Cesàro exponents or infinite-dimensional Cesàro spaces. A differently notated prior calculation remains a residual bibliographic risk.
title: Exact Dunkl--Williams constant of the two-dimensional Cesàro space
